doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: First paying gig at fourteen
summary: Pallo's first professional job at about fourteen, in a four-piece group with accordion, trumpet and drums, paid seven or fourteen dollars; he needed working papers.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Can you recall what your first paying gig was?
Yes. Wow. I think first of all the union scale was seven dollars. I think it was seven or fourteen, something like that.
That’s what they gave us, seven dollars or fourteen.
And what year would that have been?

And I was like fourteen years old. 1952 maybe or somewhere around there. ’50, ’51. And it was with a four piece group and we had an accordion player. Accordion was very popular many, many years ago. And accordion, myself on guitar, a drummer and a trumpet player. And that was the first gig — professional gig I did. I remember that.
I was about fourteen. I had to get working papers.
Someone had to drive you to the gig?
Yes. I had to have the working papers for the ABC, especially if you were working in a bar in those days. It was for the ABC and I remember doing that and it was fun.
You said this could possibly be a career for me?

It was a start and of course I wasn’t playing what I play today, which you just keep adding and adding and you never stop learning. Like yourself, you said you could see chords and you’d say wow what was that. I’ll probably play a chord and you’ll look at it and say what is it? And I’ll look at you and you’ll play something and I’ll say whoa, that sounded great.
